steps.intent: The United Kingdom's primary objective is to secure a full, sustainable renewal of the maritime interdiction mandate (targeting illicit arms, charcoal, and IED precursors to Al-Shabaab) following the short technical rollovers of resolutions 2762 and 2775. The most contentious issues during negotiations involve balancing the operational freedom of international naval interdictions with the sovereignty concerns of Somalia—which currently sits on the Council—alongside demands from Russia and China for explicit references to Somali consent, territorial integrity, and enhanced national capacity building. To preserve the 15-0-0 consensus, the draft incorporates strong language affirming Somali sovereignty, mandates prompt reporting to the Federal Government, and aligns the renewal timeline with the wider December sanctions cycle.

messages.Algeria: Algeria fully supports the renewal of the maritime interdiction provisions to degrade Al-Shabaab's operational capabilities and stem illicit arms and IED precursor flows. In line with the African Union's principled stance and our solidarity with Somalia, we must ensure full respect for Somalia's sovereignty, particularly regarding operations in its territorial waters and transparency over the final destination of seized materials. We look forward to working constructively with the penholder to adopt this resolution promptly.
messages.China: China supports the draft resolution and the renewal of the authorization to prevent illicit arms and IED materials from reaching Al-Shabaab. We emphasize that all maritime operations, particularly within Somalia's territorial waters, must fully respect Somalia's national sovereignty and territorial integrity, requiring proper consultation and consent from the Federal Government of Somalia. We also urge the international community to prioritize capacity-building assistance to help Somalia establish autonomous maritime security capabilities.
messages.Denmark: Denmark strongly supports the draft resolution renewing the maritime interdiction authorization to counter the illicit flow of weapons and IED components to Al-Shabaab. We particularly welcome the clear references to international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, as well as the emphasis on coordination with and capacity building for the Federal Government of Somalia. We stand ready to support the text as drafted.
messages.France: France welcomes the draft resolution presented by the United Kingdom to extend the maritime interdiction authorizations until 15 December 2025. Degrading Al-Shabaab's operational capabilities by disrupting the illicit trafficking of weapons, ammunition, and IED precursors remains an absolute necessity for regional stability. We fully support the current text and stand ready to vote in favor of its adoption without delay.
messages.Greece: Greece fully supports the draft resolution renewing the maritime interdiction authorizations to combat the flow of illicit weapons and IED components to Al-Shabaab. We particularly welcome the explicit reference to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) in OP2 and the emphasis on maritime security cooperation with the Federal Government of Somalia. We stand ready to vote in favour of the text as drafted.
messages.Guyana: Guyana fully supports the draft resolution renewing the maritime interdiction mandate to disrupt the illicit flow of weapons and IED components to Al-Shabaab. We particularly welcome the explicit reaffirmation of Somalia's sovereignty, adherence to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and the call for enhanced capacity-building for the Somali Navy and Coast Guard. We look forward to the swift adoption of this text.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan supports the draft resolution renewing the maritime interdiction authorizations to disrupt the flow of illicit arms and IED precursors to Al-Shabaab. We welcome the explicit reaffirmation of Somalia's sovereignty and territorial integrity, the emphasis on close coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia, and the call to enhance the capacity of the Somali Navy and Coast Guard. As a key contributor to maritime security in the Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean, Pakistan stands ready to support the swift adoption of this text.
messages.Panama: Panama fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the United Kingdom renewing the vital maritime interdiction authorizations to curb the illicit flow of weapons and IED components to Al-Shabaab. As a major maritime nation, we particularly welcome the explicit reaffirmation of international law, notably the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), as well as respect for Somalia's sovereignty and maritime capacity building. We are ready to support the adoption of the text as presented.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea fully supports the draft resolution extending the maritime interdiction mandate until 15 December 2025. Preventing the illicit flow of weapons and IED components to Al-Shabaab is critical for regional stability and maritime security, areas to which Korea actively contributes through our naval deployments in the region. We commend the United Kingdom for a well-balanced text that respects international law, including UNCLOS, while underscoring cooperation with and capacity building for the Federal Government of Somalia.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation consistently supports efforts to curtail the terrorist activities of Al-Shabaab and cut off its access to weapons and IED components. In doing so, strict respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and sovereign rights of Somalia must remain paramount, particularly regarding any activities conducted in its territorial waters. We stand ready to support the renewal of this mandate and look forward to constructive work with the penholder on the final text.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone strongly supports the renewal of the maritime interdiction mandate as a critical tool to disrupt Al-Shabaab’s financing and illicit weapons flows. In solidarity with the Federal Government of Somalia, we emphasize that international cooperation must prioritize Somali national ownership and targeted capacity-building for Somali maritime security institutions. We commend the United Kingdom's consultative approach and look forward to the swift adoption of this resolution.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the draft resolution renewing the maritime interdiction authorizations until 15 December 2025. We welcome the clear references to international law, including UNCLOS, as well as the emphasis on close cooperation with the Federal Government of Somalia and capacity-building for its maritime forces. We thank the United Kingdom for its balanced penholdership and stand ready to vote in favour of the text as drafted.
messages.Somalia: Somalia supports renewing the maritime interdiction provisions to degrade Al-Shabaab's illicit supply lines and terrorist capabilities. However, it is essential that all operations carried out within Somalia's territorial waters strictly respect our national sovereignty and take place in direct coordination with and consent of the Federal Government. We also urge international partners to prioritize sharing critical forensic and actionable intelligence with our authorities while accelerating capacity-building for our national naval and maritime law enforcement forces.
messages.United States of America: The United States strongly supports this draft resolution to renew the vital maritime interdiction authorizations through 15 December 2025. Stemming the illicit flow of lethal aid, weapons, and IED components to Al-Shabaab is indispensable for regional stability and for supporting the Federal Government of Somalia's security transition. We appreciate the United Kingdom's diligent leadership as penholder and are ready to vote in favor of the text as drafted.

steps.summary: As penholder, the United Kingdom has accommodated the shared concerns of Somalia, China, Russia, and Algeria by clarifying that inspections within Somalia's territorial waters require the consent and close coordination of the Federal Government of Somalia. We also integrated Somalia's request on sharing forensic and biometric evidence, Algeria's addition regarding the handling and disposal of seized items, and Sierra Leone's language on national ownership in OP4. The revised text preserves strong maritime interdiction capabilities while enjoying unanimous Council support.

steps.summary: All Council members expressed full support for Revision 1 without requesting any further modifications. The United Kingdom has maintained the text in its current form to ensure a smooth, unanimous adoption that renews the vital maritime interdiction mandate until 15 December 2025 while fully respecting Somalia's sovereignty and international law.

before.Somalia: Somalia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. Degradiing Al-Shabaab’s operational capacity by cutting off the illicit flow of weapons, ammunition, and improvised explosive device components remains a vital priority for the Federal Government of Somalia and for regional stability. We welcome the resolution’s strong reaffirmation of Somalia’s sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity, as well as the explicit requirement for close coordination and information-sharing with the Federal Government of Somalia regarding all maritime interdiction activities. Furthermore, we appreciate the Council's recognition of the need to strengthen the capacity of the Somali Navy and Coast Guard, ensuring that Somalia progressively assumes full responsibility for securing its maritime domain. before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr. President,

The United Kingdom is pleased to present today’s draft resolution, which renews the vital maritime interdiction authorizations until 15 December 2025.

Al-Shabaab continues to pose a grave threat to peace and security in Somalia and across the wider region. Disrupting the illicit flows of weapons, ammunition, and precursor components for improvised explosive devices into Somalia by sea remains a vital component of our collective efforts to degrade Al-Shabaab's operational capabilities and terror networks. 

This text strikes the right balance: it ensures the continuity of essential maritime interdiction operations while reaffirming full respect for Somalia's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and national ownership. It emphasizes close cooperation and information-sharing with the Federal Government of Somalia, alongside continued international support to build national maritime security capacity.

We are grateful to all Council members, and in particular the Federal Government of Somalia, for their constructive engagement throughout these negotiations. We urge all members of the Council to vote in favour of this resolution.

Thank you, Mr. President.

after.Algeria:
Mr. President,

Algeria voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, which renews the maritime interdiction mandate aimed at stemming the illicit flow of weapons, ammunition, and IED components to the terrorist group Al-Shabaab.

Algeria reaffirms its unwavering solidarity with the brotherly people and the Federal Government of Somalia in their relentless fight against terrorism. Degrading the operational capabilities and financial networks of Al-Shabaab is critical not only for the stability of Somalia, but for the peace and security of the entire region.

In supporting this resolution, Algeria underscores the paramount importance of full respect for the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence of Somalia. Maritime interdiction operations must be carried out in close consultation, coordination, and cooperation with the Federal Government of Somalia. Furthermore, timely information-sharing regarding seized vessels, weapons, and materials is essential to guarantee full transparency and support Somali judicial and security processes.

Finally, we emphasize that sustainable maritime security can only be achieved through enhanced national ownership. We urge the international community and international partners to provide the necessary support to strengthen the capacity of the Somali Navy and Coast Guard, enabling Somalia to progressively assume full control over its maritime domain.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution submitted by the United Kingdom on renewing the maritime interdiction mandate to curb illicit flows of weapons and improvised explosive device components to Al-Shabaab.

Our country consistently supports the efforts of the Federal Government of Somalia in combating the terrorist threat posed by Al-Shabaab and in restoring peace, security, and stability across the country. Severing the illicit supply chains that feed terrorist activities is an essential component of these efforts.

At the same time, we wish to reiterate that any operations carried out under this mandate must strictly respect the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of Somalia, as well as the established norms of international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea. It is essential that all interdiction activities remain closely coordinated with the Federal Government of Somalia, with full and timely sharing of all relevant information, and that the disposal of any seized materials be conducted in consultation with Mogadishu.

Furthermore, we believe it is crucial that the international community support the Federal Government of Somalia in strengthening the capacity of its own national security forces, in particular the Somali Navy and Coast Guard, so that Somalia is fully enabled to independently safeguard its own maritime domain.

Thank you.
